fluff.overview: The Dreadnought Mk II Land Train is a military conversion of the Gienah-DuraPaq Elite Series 3 civilian land train, developed by Marian Arms, Inc. on Alphard for the Marian Hegemony Armed Forces. Authorized by Hegemony Armed Forces commander Michael Alexander and supervised by Marian Arms technician Proculeius Lodi, the project sought to transform the Hegemony's essential ore transport vehicles into self-defending convoy platforms capable of protecting critical supply routes without diverting dedicated combat assets to escort duty. Development began in 3072 and formal introduction was achieved in 3081. Consisting of a heavily armed tractor module and a series of interchangeable armed trailer configurations, the Mk II represents one of the Hegemony's most ambitious military engineering efforts. Only two complete trains were ever constructed, making the Dreadnought Mk II among the rarest vehicles in Periphery service.
fluff.capabilities:
Each Dreadnought Mk II trailer is an unpowered 50-ton tracked module towed and powered by the tractor unit. The modules draw motive power directly from the tractor's fusion engine, requiring no independent power plant of their own. Built on a commercial Elite Series 3 trailer chassis upgraded with Tech D armor, each module carries four and a half tons of commercial grade ATC armor rated at BAR 7, substantially heavier than the civilian baseline. The modules are interconnectable, allowing the train to be assembled in varying consists by linking modules to each other as well as directly to the tractor.

Each module carries a twenty-ton cargo bay with four access doors on the front, left, right, and rear sides. The cargo carried varies by configuration, with each trailer variant equipped for a specific type of freight. Trailer gunners are quartered aboard the tractor and move to their stations when action is called. All weapon systems are governed by Advanced Fire Control. Individual modules are regularly exchanged between Train 838 and Train 520, allowing the two trains to vary their weapon fits and cargo assignments as mission requirements change across Alphard's mining routes.
fluff.deployment: Configuration Three mounts an Extended LRM-5 paired with a Streak SRM-6 in its turret, both governed by Advanced Fire Control. The Streak guidance system improves hit probability against maneuvering targets, making this configuration well-suited to engagements against faster raider vehicles. Six gunners crew this configuration, reflecting the heavier crew demand of its weapons suite. Its twenty-ton cargo bay carries just over seventeen tons of refrigerated materials, supporting the Hegemony's food distribution network on Alphard's longer routes. Train 520 routinely operates two Configuration Three trailers, pairing them with Configuration Four modules for a consist balancing precision missile fire with direct autocannon capability.
fluff.history:
The Marian Hegemony's overland transport network has been essential to its economy since the realm's founding, with land trains ferrying ore from Alphard's distant mining fields to Nova Roma and the industrial centers supporting Marian military power. The Gienah-DuraPaq Elite Series 3 became the standard platform for this role, and by the mid-thirty-first century the Hegemony operated substantial convoys of these vehicles across Alphard's varied terrain. As the Hegemony grew from a mining operation into a Periphery power attracting raider interest, the vulnerability of these lightly defended convoys became an increasing liability.

The Word of Blake's terrorist attacks on Nova Roma in the 3060s disrupted supply shipments and rendered several convoy routes untenable. When the Blakists returned the following year and Lugdunum became a primary target, the Hegemony found itself unable to spare military assets for convoy escort. Caesar Cassius O'Reilly's response upon assuming the throne was to appoint Proculeius Lodi of Marian Arms to develop a permanent solution, commissioning a full military conversion of the Elite Series 3 platform rather than relying on improvised escort arrangements.

Lodi's program, begun in 3072, worked closely with HAF commander Michael Alexander to develop specifications for what would become the Dreadnought Mk II. In September 3079, O'Reilly met with Lodi and Alexander in closed session, reviewed the progress of the project, and approved an ambitious upgrade to the design's defensive and offensive capabilities. O'Reilly provided a generous development budget, reflecting the strategic importance the Hegemony placed on protecting its mining infrastructure.

By the late 3070s the Mk II was undergoing field trials on Alphard, with life returning to normal in the Hegemony as the two prototype trains demonstrated the viability of the armed land train concept. Train 838 and Train 520 completed their trials and entered service in 3081. FrontierTech marketed the design as both a military asset and a commercial investment opportunity for potential outside customers, though no additional units beyond the two original trains were confirmed constructed.
